title: Over the past decade, North Korea has trained around 4,000 Africans in military tactics, with experts currently stationed in 11 African countries. While France and Cuba are often highlighted for their military presence in Africa, North Korea's role is significant yet frequently overlooked. The DPRK has provided military training and equipment to various nations, including Zimbabwe, where their involvement has been met with mixed reviews. Despite initial praise from Zimbabwe's Prime Minister Robert Mugabe, the effectiveness of North Korean training has been questioned, particularly regarding the performance of the 5th brigade in military operations. The brigade's lack of success in engagements, such as those in Mozambique and Matabeleland, has led to a general disillusionment with North Korean military assistance, culminating in a shift towards training from British and Zimbabwean officers.
